title: Project Entry Point
description: The Django management script is the command-line entry point for the entire labConnect backend. It defaults to the dev settings module, which means running any management command — migrations, the dev server, or the custom `runlan` command for LAN-accessible mobile development — starts here. Understanding this file tells you how the backend is bootstrapped and which settings environment is active by default.

title: Infrastructure and Deployment
description: Before reading a single line of application code, it helps to understand how the system is packaged and deployed. The Dockerfile builds a single-stage container image that installs Python and system dependencies (including GeoDjango's GDAL/GEOS libraries), copies the project, and starts Gunicorn on port 8000 as a non-root user. The docker-compose.yml runs a companion PostgreSQL 15 database with a named volume and a pg_isready health check — exactly the PostGIS-enabled database the Django ORM requires. The render.yaml blueprint automates production deployment to Render.com using Supabase Postgres, bridging development containers to cloud hosting without changing application code.

title: Django Settings and App Configuration
description: The split settings package (`base.py` → `dev.py` / `prod.py`) is the control plane for the entire platform. Base.py configures the PostGIS database backend, DRF with RS256-signed JWTs, Celery with Redis, Django Channels for WebSocket readiness, MinIO for file storage, CORS origins, and brute-force protection via django-axes. Dev.py overrides JWT to HS256 (no RSA keys needed locally) and opens CORS to all LAN IP ranges so Expo Go on a phone can reach the backend over Wi-Fi. Prod.py locks everything down with HTTPS-only cookies, HSTS, and WhiteNoise static serving. The root URL configuration in `urls.py` is the single file that wires all app routers under `/api/v1/` and also mounts the Swagger UI and ReDoc endpoints.

title: Shared Data Foundation
description: All Django app models in this project inherit from `core/models.py`'s `BaseModel` abstract class, which provides UUIDs for external IDs (safe to expose in URLs and APIs), a BigAutoField integer for internal primary keys (fast for joins), soft-delete via an `is_active` flag, and an `ActiveManager` that filters deleted records out by default. This single class appears as a fan-in dependency of every domain model in the project — accounts, laboratories, analyses, appointments, inventory, and notifications all build on it. Understanding BaseModel means you understand the structural contract every table in the database honors.

title: Identity and Authentication Models
description: The `accounts/models.py` file defines the identity layer that everything else depends on. The custom `User` model uses phone number as the primary identifier (instead of Django's default username), with email as an optional secondary. `PatientProfile` and `StaffProfile` extend it through OneToOne relationships, keeping patient-specific data (CNAM number, blood type) and staff-specific data (laboratory FK, role) separate from the core auth record. `OTPCode` stores hashed, expiring codes for phone verification. `TrustedDevice` persists biometric device tokens so patients and nurses can log in with Face ID or fingerprint after a first successful OTP verification. The `managers.py` file normalizes phone numbers on creation and supports both regular and superuser flows.

title: Role-Based Permission System
description: The platform supports six roles — `lab_chief`, `biologist`, `technician`, `nurse`, `secretary`, and `patient` — implemented as Django Groups rather than a custom permission model. The `core/permissions.py` file is the most-imported file in the entire backend (fan-in of 8), defining the `HasRole` base class, shortcut permission classes (`IsPatient`, `IsNurse`, `IsLabChief`, etc.), a 2FA verification guard for sensitive staff operations, and the `current_lab_id()` request helper that extracts which lab the JWT bearer belongs to. This file is the keystone of the API security model — every ViewSet uses at least one of its classes. The `seed_roles.py` management command bootstraps these Django Groups from scratch on a fresh install.

title: Authentication API and Services
description: The authentication surface is split across three view files to keep concerns clear. `views.py` handles OTP request/verify for patients, email login for staff, Google OAuth for both roles, and Firebase JWT login for mobile. `views_biometric.py` handles device enrollment and biometric login using the hashed device tokens from `TrustedDevice`. `views_totp.py` handles TOTP 2FA setup for staff via pyotp, including QR code generation for authenticator apps. Behind these views, `services/otp.py` abstracts OTP delivery with pluggable providers (Mock for dev, Twilio SMS or WhatsApp for production), and `services/firebase.py` validates Firebase ID tokens by fetching and caching Google's public RSA certificates.

title: Core Domain Models: Labs, Appointments, Analyses
description: Three models form the heart of the clinical workflow. `laboratories/models.py` defines the `Laboratory` entity with a PostGIS `Point` field for geospatial queries, a JSON `opening_hours` field, home-visit fee settings, CNAM support flag, and a slug. `appointments/models.py` builds on `BaseModel` and references both `Laboratory` and `User`, adding `VisitType` (clinic vs. home) and `AppointmentStatus` enumerations, a GIS location field for home visits, an `assigned_nurse` FK, and a fee calculation method. `analyses/models.py` captures the clinical detail: `TestCatalogEntry` defines what tests the lab offers with CNAM coverage and questionnaire support; `Sample` tracks the physical specimen with barcode and lifecycle status; `TestOrder` links a test to an appointment with CNAM cost split; `TestResult` stores the technician-entered value and biologist-validated result with a full audit trail.

title: API Layer: ViewSets and Serializers
description: The API layer exposes the domain models to clients through DRF ViewSets paired with serializers. `analyses/views.py` is the most complex ViewSet (fan-out of 5), implementing catalog management, sample reception, result entry, biologist validation, patient result listing, PDF streaming, walk-in registration, statistics, and invoice generation — all role-gated via `core/permissions.py`. `appointments/views.py` handles status-change transitions that cascade: confirming an appointment creates Sample records; completing a home visit triggers nurse assignment logic. The `notifications/events.py` file (fan-in of 2) is called by both the analyses and appointments ViewSets to emit `Notification` records whenever appointment lifecycle events or result validations occur, ensuring all relevant users receive in-app messages without a WebSocket layer.

title: PDF Generation and Result Reports
description: When a biologist validates a test result, the backend can generate a structured A4 PDF using `analyses/pdf.py`, which is built on ReportLab Platypus. The report includes patient identity, the test result value alongside its reference range, a clinical context section, and a biologist signature block. The `analyses/views.py` PDF endpoint streams this file directly to the caller, which on the web dashboard triggers a browser download and on the mobile app is caught by `frontend-client/src/pdfDownload.js`, written to Expo's file cache as base64, and opened in the native share sheet so patients can save, print, or forward their results.

title: Web Staff Dashboard
description: The React 19 + Vite staff dashboard is structured around three pillars that appear in the highest fan-in rankings. `api.js` (fan-in 16) is imported by every screen and component that touches the backend — it owns JWT storage, automatic token refresh on 401 responses, and all domain-specific fetch functions. `constants.js` (fan-in 10) centralizes role definitions, permission maps, and category lists, ensuring role-gating logic is consistent across all screens. `App.jsx` (fan-out 16) is the routing hub: the `Gate` component checks whether the user has a lab assigned (redirecting to `Onboarding.jsx` if not), and the `Shell` component renders the `Sidebar` and `Topbar` layout before delegating to the active screen based on the user's current role.

title: Key Staff Screens: Dashboard and Analyses
description: The two most visited staff screens encapsulate the day-to-day lab workflow. `Dashboard.jsx` shows today's appointment list, allows walk-in creation via `WalkInModal` (which queries the test catalog and handles CNAM configuration), surfaces the `AppointmentDetailModal` for status progression, and embeds `FinanceTab` for daily revenue and CNAM reimbursement tracking. `Analyses.jsx` is where the clinical work happens: technicians enter results through a `ResultEntryModal`, biologists validate them through a `ValidationModal`, and all users can download the PDF report. These two screens together reflect the full appointment-to-result lifecycle that `appointments/views.py` and `analyses/views.py` back on the server.

title: Mobile App: Patient and Nurse Journeys
description: The React Native (Expo 54) mobile app serves two very different users through role-based navigation. `App.js` switches between a patient tab navigator (Home, Bookings, Profile) and a nurse tab navigator (Route, Profile) based on the authenticated user's role. On the patient side, `HomeScreen.js` lets patients search labs by name, city, or analysis code with map-based geo-filtering; `LabDetailScreen.js` shows the test catalog; and `CartScreen.js` handles booking with a date/slot picker, home-visit mode toggle, CNAM coverage breakdown, and a prerequisite questionnaire. On the nurse side, `NurseRouteScreen.js` shows a vertical timeline of today's home visits; `NurseCollectScreen.js` handles per-tube barcode entry; and `NurseValidateScreen.js` closes the visit with a finger-signature canvas backed by `PanResponder` — no external SVG dependency required.

title: Mobile Auth and Biometric Login
description: The mobile authentication layer mirrors the backend's multi-method support. `auth.js` is the React Context provider that wraps the app — it exposes `loginWithOTP`, `loginWithEmail`, `loginWithGoogle`, `loginWithBiometric`, and `logout`, hydrating user state from the backend on mount. Biometric authentication is handled by `biometric.js`, which bridges three Expo packages: `expo-local-authentication` triggers the OS biometric prompt, `expo-crypto` generates a stable device ID, and `expo-secure-store` persists the device token and phone number between sessions. After a patient's first successful OTP login, the app prompts them to enable Face ID or fingerprint for all future logins, using the `TrustedDevice` model on the backend to store the hashed token.

title: Inventory Management
description: The inventory subsystem tracks the lab's reagents, consumables, and equipment through two tightly related models. `inventory/models.py` defines `InventoryItem` (with category, unit cost, minimum stock threshold, and the computed `is_low_stock` property) and `InventoryMovement`, which records signed-delta stock changes atomically using `SELECT FOR UPDATE` to prevent race conditions under concurrent use. The `views.py` enforces role-based access — lab chiefs, technicians, and biologists can add or edit items, but only the lab chief can delete them. On the web dashboard, `Inventory.jsx` presents this as a table with inline `ItemModal` and `MovementModal` for CRUD and stock recording, completing the operational picture that the API model backs.
